“Freedom, Alvah, freedom.” 

On May 7, 1943, Ayn Rand’s “The Fountainhead” was first published.

Commemorative passports for America’s 250th … featuring a living president? Cato’s Dan Greenberg argues public office isn’t a branding opportunity—and we should bar naming/placing living elected officials on public buildings and documents. 
ow.ly/kawv50YVOJ9

How can America unleash the next energy revolution? 

On May 13, the Cato Institute will host Secretary of Energy @SecretaryWright to discuss the current state of energy policy — and what's to come. 

Register and follow the conversation live: ow.ly/531a50YWccs

AI investment is acting as a massive tailwind for US economic growth. And it is being fueled by imports entering almost entirely tariff-free, explain Cato’s scholars. 

ow.ly/ZGUs50YW0AN

Introducing the Cato Innovation Project!
 
You propose your own full-time job. Cato funds it. We make it happen together.
 
Learn more and apply: cato.org/innovation

Video

The Cato Institute is proud to announce that two of its scholars have been named to @washingtonian magazine’s 2026 list of the “500 Most Influential People Shaping Policy” in Washington, DC. 
 
The Cato scholars recognized this year:
🔹 @David_J_Bier, Director of Immigration Studies and The Selz Foundation Chair in Immigration Policy. 
🔹 @mfcannon, Director of Health Policy Studies. 
 
ow.ly/X7GQ50YWaY7

A proposed federal bill restricting institutional investors in the housing market hasn't passed Congress yet — but the damage is already unfolding. Cato's Stephen Slivinski and Norbert Michel argue this is precisely why Washington should stay out of housing markets and let the market work. 

ow.ly/Y11z50YVNKi

Spirit Airlines’ closure is a cautionary tale: block mergers and flirt with price caps, and consumers can end up with fewer low-cost options—all at the expense of people losing their jobs, explains Cato’s @EconWithNick.

ow.ly/v1Qa50YVAiK

The War Powers Resolution no longer works. It’s time to put it to rest and start from scratch on a new tool to check the modern American president, says Cato’s @katherinet57.

ow.ly/kjGU50YVNqG

People call methadone a life sentence, a ball and chain. In a new Cato Podcast episode, @dr4liberty talks with Helen Redmond, author of “Liquid Handcuffs,” about how a Nixon-era crime control program became America’s dominant addiction treatment model, and why people with addiction should be able to access methadone directly from health care providers.

Listen on Apple, Spotify, and our website!
 
Apple: ow.ly/UIhS50YVISp 
Spotify: ow.ly/cOVU50YVISs 
Our website: ow.ly/tyvi50YVISJ

Learn more: o

As America turns 250, “Proclaiming Liberty” by @TimothySandefur revisits the revolutionary year of 1776 through the minds of John Adams and Thomas Jefferson. 
  
The ideal read before July 4th. Order your copy today! 
cato.org/books/proclaiming-l…

Video

The Trump administration reportedly is considering vetting AI tools before they are released. This precautionary approach threatens free expression just as it did when the Biden administration took this path, says Cato’s @dr_inserra.

Federal power is enumerated, not unlimited. Yet prosecutors tried to stretch a stadium flare incident into a 7-year federal “arson” charge—until a judge pushed back. Cato’s @foxmike90 argues an ever-expanding view of federal authority undermines federalism. 

ow.ly/NuGQ50YVfTI

Friends of the Cato Institute came out in force for the Cato on Tour event at the Harvard Club. 

If you weren't there, you missed a timely dialogue with Cato's @ConLawWarrior, @David_J_Bier, Harrison Moar, @johanknorberg, and President Peter Goettler about how executive power is expanding—and how we can defend liberty. 

To get up to speed, check out our Vision for Liberty Campaign: ow.ly/nCa750YVB0U

Thank you to everyone who joined us. We'll be back in NYC in the fall with more.

Join us for an expert event, discussing reform strategies that address the program’s structural flaws and prevent Social Security from worsening the debt crisis. Featuring Cato's @RominaBoccia, @JessicaBRiedl of the Brookings Institute, and @EugeneSteuerle of the Urban Institute. nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1qxoNegyM…

The SEC’s “Gag Rule” forces people who settle cases to stay silent forever—even if the agency is wrong. That’s not a free choice; it’s pressure. Critics say it violates free speech and want the Supreme Court to strike it down.

ow.ly/Zsxt50YVf3I

Join us for a conversation with leading European voices on the future of digital taxation. 

Featuring: Cato’s @adamnmichel, @ahellmanndc of the Tholos Foundation, @crisberechet of Tax Foundation Europe, and @MatBauerEcon of the European Centre for International Political Economy.
nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1YxNrZqkP…
